# pushsecurity_custom_detections (Data Source)

Lists the custom detections in the tenant.

The API's index returns identity only, so this data source does the same: it tells you what exists, not what each detection does. Use it to find detections that are not yet managed by Terraform.

## Example Usage

```terraform
data "pushsecurity_custom_detections" "all" {}

# Every custom detection in the tenant, by the identifier you import it with.
output "detection_names" {
  value = {
    for d in data.pushsecurity_custom_detections.all.detections :
    d.detection_event_type => d.name
  }
}

# The detections you already manage. In your own configuration, reference the
# resources instead, as in
# pushsecurity_custom_detection.torrent_website_visit.detection_event_type.
locals {
  managed_detection_event_types = []
}

# Useful for finding detections that exist in the tenant but are not yet
# managed by Terraform.
output "unmanaged_detections" {
  value = setsubtract(
    data.pushsecurity_custom_detections.all.detection_event_types,
    local.managed_detection_event_types,
  )
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Read-Only

- `detection_event_types` (Set of String) Just the identifiers, for convenience in `for_each` and in `contains` checks.
- `detections` (Attributes List) Every custom detection in the tenant, as the API returns them. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--detections))

<a id="nestedatt--detections"></a>
### Nested Schema for `detections`

Read-Only:

- `detection_event_type` (String) The detection's permanent identifier, and the value to use when importing it.
- `name` (String) The detection's name.
